text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- New flood danger for Oderbruch area as water levels reach record highs.
- Members of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats and the liberal Free Democrats want to stop talk about future of their coalition.
- Construction Minister Klaus Toepfer says there wil be no cuts in town planning spending next year.
- Interest rates for home loans reach new lows.
HANDELSBLATT
- Experts predict DAX share index could move above 5,000 points in the medium term.
- Government and opposition politicians demand reduction in Germany's contributions to the European Union.
- Saxony state premier Kurt Biedenkopf raises possibility of a five-year delay for single European currency.
- German Confederation of Industry president Hans-Olaf Henkel calls on government and opposition to agree soon on tax reform plans.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Ruling coalition hints that talks with opposition on tax reform will fail.
- Jan Ullrich becomes first German to win Tour de France.
- Music industry fears Internet could endanger future of the compact disc.
- Economic situation in the European construction industry recovering from low point, Ifo economic institute says.
- West Germans pay twice as much tax as east Germans on average, Ifo survey says.
DIE WELT
- 20,000 people on flood alert in eastern Germany.
- Federal Labour Office president Bernhard Jagoda calls for more flexibility in apprenticeship system.
- German banks' half-year results point to record full-year figures.
- Experts call for reform of pensions system to take place earlier than planned.
